findings.passage: 80% of Wisconsin voters support universal background checks for the purchase of firearms. That’s because the vast majority of Wisconsinites are responsible with their firearms, but they understand that a level of trust must be understood before a purchaser is allowed to take a gun home with them. I have heard from constituents with firsthand knowledge of how children drawn into gang activities are able to acquire guns because of the gun-show loophole.
findings.note: Press statement issued in his name about the governor's special session on gun violence; he backs background checks on all gun purchases and refers to a gun-show loophole. Copy of his release on Urban Milwaukee.

findings.passage: Under due process, if a court finds the reasons of a person’s family to be credible, the court would remove firearms from that person temporarily. Other states that have passed these Extreme Risk Protection Orders, or “red flag” laws have seen a reduction in the rate of firearm suicides.
findings.note: Same release; he describes court-ordered temporary removal of guns (red-flag orders) and cites lower firearm suicide rates in other states. He also calls on the Senate to debate and vote on the two bills in the special session.
